newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian cement industry to expand outside Java.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian cement industry to expand outside Java.

text.p: Indonesia will expand its cement industry outside the most populous island of Java by the year 2003 due to environmental concerns, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.

The agency quoted Soepardjo, chairman of the Indonesian Cement Association (ASI), as saying the cement industry would expand outside Java because the environmental capacity of the island could not support increased production.
With the demand for cement growing at 12 percent per year, Java could not satisfy this need by 2003, he said. More than 60 percent of the country's almost 200 million people live in Java.
Antara gave no other details, but quoted Soepardjo as saying Indonesia's cement production would have an excess supply of 2.0 million tonnes in 1997.
The private PT Cipta Cakra Murdaya said in December it planned to build a cement plant in central Sulawesi to start production by 2000 with an annual output of 3.0 million tonnes.
